problem: Find a basis of the null space of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
To find a basis of $\text{Null}(A),$ we need to solve the equation $Ax=0$ and express the solution as a linear combination of linearly independent vectors. Those vectors form a basis of $\text{Null}(A).$

The given matrix is already in row echelon form. So, the equation $Ax=0$ corresponds to the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

This implies that the only solution of $Ax=0$ is $x=0.$ So, $\text{Null}(A)={0},$ which means that the basis of $\text{Null}(A)$ is the empty set, i.e., $B={\,}.$
